amends: PREREG.json and amend-1 to amend-3 are NOT changed and no floor in them is lowered. Registers the response to the delta review of add7c86 (reviews/ingest-delta/review-1.md: N1, N2, N3, F2). Committed alone, before any change to scan.py, the ingester, the tap or the oracle, and before any run of the fresh held-out set.
output_dir: ingest/results4 (new). results, results2 and results3 are kept unchanged as the record for earlier commits. results4 comes from ONE stamped run on a clean committed tree and supersedes results3 for every claim.

A1_N1_alignment_contract.finding: Prior history [user yes, assistant ok]; the host then sends [user yes, user new] with no retry_of. Longest-common-run alignment gives start 0, length 1, one tie: only 'new' is emitted, the newly authored 'yes' disappears, no ambiguity is raised and claim_exactly_once() can be true.
A1_N1_alignment_contract.contract: (1) Explicit boundary: tap.call(request, stream=False, retry_of=None, new_count=None). new_count is the number of trailing messages of THIS request that are new to the log. It is recorded in the REQ body. When the host supplies a valid new_count (an integer, 0 to the request length) the ingester uses it and never infers: messages before the boundary are not request events (an unseen one is recorded once as host-authored), messages from the boundary on are request events. An invalid value is ignored and recorded (port event boundary_claim_ignored) and inference applies. (2) No boundary: alignment is accepted silently ONLY when provably unambiguous: the request has no repeated message key, the alignment is the unique maximal run, every message of the aligned run occurs exactly once in the ingested history, the aligned run ends at the end of the history, and every unaligned message is unseen. Otherwise the ingester does not guess: it emits every message that could be new (from the first message that is unaligned or repeats a known key to the end of the request), flags those events ambiguous_repeat, opens a BLOCKING gap ambiguous_alignment, and claim_complete() and claim_exactly_once() are false for the stream. (3) Visibility: every use of a host declaration (retry_of or new_count) is a port event AND is listed in completeness()['declared_calls'], and the response events of that call carry the declaration in their meta, so it is visible in the ordinary events() view.
A1_N1_alignment_contract.assumptions_stated_in_claims: A host that declares retry_of or new_count is honest and correct; the ingester cannot check it (a wrong new_count drops or duplicates messages and only the declared_calls list shows it).
A1_N1_alignment_contract.tests: ingest/tests/test_delta2.py. Failing-first on add7c86: the reviewer's case (both user events present, flagged, blocking gap, both claims false); the same case with new_count=2 (both events, exact, claims true, call in declared_calls); more than one new message per call under repeating content with and without the boundary; undeclared identical resend is now a blocking flagged duplicate; declared suppression visible in completeness.
A1_N1_alignment_contract.item_13_rerun: Repeated-content hosts as in amend-3 A3 (3 patterns x windows 4, 6, 8 x 2 providers, 20 calls = 18 runs) in two arms. Arm A, host supplies new_count: 18/18 equal to the host oracle, 0 blocking gaps, claim_exactly_once true. Arm B, no boundary: 18/18 contain every oracle event (multiset superset, no loss), every run carries a blocking ambiguous_alignment gap and claim_exactly_once is false; the number of extra flagged events is reported. A new item 13c adds hosts that append 2 or 3 new messages per call under repeating content (patterns same and alt, windows 6 and 8, both providers = 8 runs), both arms, same pass rule. Unique-text hosts (item 11, item 7, scripted conversations, item 13 unique): zero ambiguity gaps and equal to the oracle.

A2_N2_payload_oracle.finding: The host oracle reduced tool calls and results to their ids, so a defect that keeps the id and corrupts the payload passed.
A2_N2_payload_oracle.fix: The oracle tuple gains a normalised payload: for a tool call the tool name and the arguments as canonical JSON; for a tool result the result content as text; for thinking the signature. It is derived at the host from provider message structure by code in proofs_common that does not use shapes.blocks_of_message or the ingester. The event side is projected from the stored event content by independent code. The old id-only projection is kept as legacy_event_tuples to show what it cannot see.
A2_N2_payload_oracle.control: CorruptPayloadIngester (controls.py): preserves every tool id and replaces tool arguments and tool-result content with empty values. Item 2g: 20 seeds x 2 providers = 40 runs of the item-2a delivery shape. Floors: the legacy id-only projection equals the oracle's id-only view in >=36 of 40 runs (the old oracle cannot see it) AND the payload oracle reports a mismatch in >=36 of 40 runs.
A2_N2_payload_oracle.wording: Until this passes, results are described as equality of the specified tuple projection.

A3_F2_scanner_and_fresh_heldout.burned: The held-out set of add7c86 (ingest/heldout.py HELDOUT, seed0 9) and the tuned set are used to repair ingest/scan.py and are therefore labelled BURNED for the held-out role. They are still scored, labelled burned, so old and new figures can be compared.
A3_F2_scanner_and_fresh_heldout.process: Order is fixed: (1) this amendment and ingest/heldout2.py (the fresh set generator, its scoring and its benign generator) are committed alone; (2) scan.py is changed WITHOUT running heldout2.py on any scanner and without printing any of its examples (only a different seed is used to smoke-test the generator's code paths, and only counts of strings are inspected); (3) the fresh set is scored ONCE, inside the single stamped run, in the item named item12c, together with the tuned and burned sets. No scanner edit follows that run.

fresh_heldout_rule.seed: SEED = first 8 hex digits of SHA-256 of the ASCII string 'fresh-heldout|add7c86881ae2793ec32ecc3fa0f79dfd8d8add4' read as an integer. It is derived from the base commit id, a value that cannot be tuned against.
fresh_heldout_rule.families: sk (a vendor-style live key with a 24-character random part), aws (an access key id), ghp (a source-host personal token with a 36-character random part), bearer (an Authorization Bearer header with a 40-character token), pwkv (a password key-value pair with a 14-character value), pem (a private-key block of three 64-character body lines between header and footer lines).
fresh_heldout_rule.transforms: identity, base64, base64_wrap24 (base64 broken into 24-character lines), hex_lower, dot_split (dot between every character), tab_split (tab between every character), percent (percent-encoding of every byte), base32_lower (lower-case base32).
fresh_heldout_rule.cells: 24 of the 48 (family, transform) cells chosen by random.Random(SEED).sample over the list ordered family-major as written above.
fresh_heldout_rule.size: 40 examples per cell (960 examples). Example i of a cell uses random.Random('%d|%s|%s|%d' % (SEED, family, transform, i)). Text is 'note: <transformed credential> end'.
fresh_heldout_rule.predicate: complete_redaction as in amend-3 A2 with K=8. Sensitive strings: the transformed credential (not for identity) and the random part of the credential (each body line for pem; the header line is also sensitive for pem).
fresh_heldout_rule.benign: 18 classes x 40 examples: the 12 classes of heldout.BENIGN with the same seed rule, plus 6 new classes (certificate block, public-key block, known-hosts line, data-URI of random bytes, changelog line, SQL statement), each carried as 'note: <x> ok'. Metric: fraction of examples that redact_text changes. No floor.

A3_F2_scanner_and_fresh_heldout.reporting: Single artifact item12c reports, for each of tuned set, burned held-out and fresh held-out: detected, whole_string_absent and complete_redaction counts with Wilson 95% lower bounds, per-class and per-cell; the fresh benign false-positive rate; and the old scanner's figures at add7c86 (tuned 400/400, burned held-out 300/800 under complete redaction) beside them. No floor is set. The fresh figure is the only held-out claim; the burned figure is shown for comparison only. The fresh set is still synthetic and positive-only; it is not deployment recall.
A3_F2_scanner_and_fresh_heldout.item5: The on-disk persistence check (item 5) is re-scored with a fragment predicate: a covered run fails when any contiguous 8-character fragment of any needle (the encoded variant, the plain secret without its fixed prefix, and their JSON-escaped forms) occurs in any file of the database directory. The old whole-string figure is kept next to it.
A3_F2_scanner_and_fresh_heldout.claim_wording: heldout.py's opening statement is reduced to what the repository can show; no independence of the generator from tuning is asserted.
